subject: Political Science (Code: 323)
past_paper_reference: CUET UG Political Science Past Papers (2022-2024)

questions.question: What was the official election symbol of the Indian National Congress during the first two General Elections of 1952 and 1957?
options: A) Two bullocks with a yoke on
questions.explanation: During the first general elections in the 1950s, the Congress contested under the election symbol of 'two bullocks with a yoke on'.

questions.question: Which opposition political party had the electoral symbol of a lighted earthen lamp (Deepa) during the first general elections?
questions.explanation: The Bharatiya Jana Sangh, founded in 1951 by Shyama Prasad Mukherjee, adopted the lighted earthen oil lamp (Deepa) as its election symbol.

questions.question: Who served as the president of the All India Muslim League who led the campaign for the partition of British India and the creation of Pakistan?
questions.explanation: Muhammad Ali Jinnah led the Muslim League's demand for a separate homeland for Muslims, advocating the Two-Nation Theory.

questions.question: Which British lawyer was appointed as the Chairman of the two Boundary Commissions tasked with drawing the international borders between India and Pakistan in 1947?
questions.explanation: Sir Cyril Radcliffe headed the Boundary Commissions that demarcated the Radcliffe Line dividing Punjab and Bengal between India and Pakistan in 1947.

questions.question: What title was officially held by the hereditary monarchical ruler of the princely state of Hyderabad prior to its integration into India?
questions.explanation: The ruler of Hyderabad held the title of the Nizam (Mir Osman Ali Khan was the last ruling Nizam) and was among the world's richest individuals.

questions.question: Which state was the first linguistic state to be created in independent India in December 1952?
questions.explanation: Andhra State was carved out of the Telugu-speaking areas of Madras State in December 1952 following Potti Sreeramulu's fast unto death.

questions.question: Who serves as the ex-officio Chairman of the National Development Council (NDC) of India?
options: C) The Prime Minister of India
D) The Governor of the Reserve Bank of India
questions.explanation: The Prime Minister of India serves as the ex-officio Chairman of the National Development Council, which includes Union Cabinet ministers and state Chief Ministers.

questions.question: In the Second Five Year Plan, the state adopted an industrialization strategy that prioritized which type of industries?
options: D) Heavy and basic capital goods industries
questions.explanation: The Second Plan, drafted under P.C. Mahalanobis, concentrated public investment on heavy capital-goods industries such as steel, heavy machinery, and power generation.

questions.question: The revolutionary dairy development initiative known as 'Operation Flood' was organized around which cooperative brand centered in Anand, Gujarat?
questions.explanation: Operation Flood was built upon the cooperative dairy architecture pioneered by the Anand Milk Union Limited (Amul) in Gujarat.

questions.question: Which of the following leaders was NOT one of the five founding pioneers of the Non-Aligned Movement (NAM) in 1961?
options: C) Josip Broz Tito of Yugoslavia
D) Gamal Abdel Nasser of Egypt
questions.explanation: The five founders of NAM were Nehru (India), Tito (Yugoslavia), Nasser (Egypt), Sukarno (Indonesia), and Kwame Nkrumah (Ghana). Mao Zedong was not a founder.

questions.question: The Panchsheel agreement of 1954 was signed between India and which neighboring country?
options: C) The People's Republic of China
questions.explanation: Panchsheel (Five Principles of Peaceful Coexistence) was signed between Indian Prime Minister Nehru and Chinese Premier Zhou Enlai on 29 April 1954.

questions.question: Which Soviet city served as the venue for the signing of the January 1966 peace declaration between India and Pakistan following the 1965 war?
questions.explanation: Prime Minister Lal Bahadur Shastri and President Ayub Khan signed the Tashkent Declaration in Tashkent (then Soviet Uzbekistan) on 10 January 1966.

questions.sub_topic: Challenge to and Restoration of Congress System
questions.question: In the Congress presidential election of 1969, who was the official nominee chosen by the Syndicate whom Indira Gandhi opposed?
questions.explanation: The Syndicate nominated Neelam Sanjiva Reddy, while Indira Gandhi endorsed independent candidate V.V. Giri, calling upon MPs and MLAs for a 'conscience vote'.

questions.sub_topic: Challenge to and Restoration of Congress System
questions.question: What was the popular slogan coined by the Grand Alliance opposition coalition in the 1971 General Election to counter Indira Gandhi?
questions.explanation: The Grand Alliance campaigned on the single-point agenda of 'Indira Hatao', to which Indira Gandhi famously countered with 'Garibi Hatao' (Remove Poverty).

questions.sub_topic: Challenge to and Restoration of Congress System
questions.question: What were the 'Privy Purses' that Indira Gandhi's government successfully abolished through a constitutional amendment in 1971?
options: A) Secret campaign donation funds managed by commercial banks
B) Pensions granted to retired British colonial civil servants
C) Government-guaranteed hereditary pensions and privy allowances paid to the former rulers of princely states
D) Subsidies allocated exclusively to private textile mill owners
questions.explanation: Privy purses were hereditary state payments guaranteed to princely rulers at the time of accession, abolished by the 26th Constitutional Amendment in 1971.

questions.question: Which veteran Gandhian and socialist leader emerged out of retirement in 1974 to lead the student movement in Bihar against corruption and inflation?
questions.explanation: Jayaprakash Narayan (JP) accepted the leadership of the Bihar student movement in 1974, transforming it into a mass civil disobedience movement for 'Total Revolution'.

questions.question: In which city did socialist leader George Fernandes organize the massive May 1974 strike of railway employees?
options: A) Across India as a nationwide strike (led from Delhi)
questions.explanation: George Fernandes led the 20-day nationwide Railway Strike in May 1974 through the National Coordination Committee for Railwaymen's Struggle (NCCRS).

questions.question: Who served as the Prime Minister of India heading the Janata Party government when the National Emergency was officially lifted and elections were held in 1977?
questions.explanation: Morarji Desai became India's first non-Congress Prime Minister in March 1977 after the Janata Party won a resounding victory post-Emergency.

questions.question: Which regional political party led the autonomy agitation in Punjab during the 1970s and 1980s and adopted the Anandpur Sahib Resolution?
questions.explanation: The Shiromani Akali Dal adopted the Anandpur Sahib Resolution in 1973, demanding federal restructuring and greater provincial autonomy for Punjab.

questions.question: Which student organisation spearheaded the six-year-long anti-foreigner agitation in Assam between 1979 and 1985?
questions.explanation: The All Assam Students Union (AASU) led the popular mass movement against illegal Bangladeshi immigrants from 1979 until the 1985 Assam Accord.

questions.question: Who headed the Second Backward Classes Commission whose report recommended 27% reservation in central government jobs for OBCs?
questions.explanation: B.P. Mandal (Bindeshwari Prasad Mandal) chaired the Second Backward Classes Commission appointed by the Janata Party government in 1978.

questions.question: Which political party was founded by Kanshi Ram in 1984 to mobilize Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and Other Backward Classes?
questions.explanation: Kanshi Ram established the Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) on 14 April 1984 to secure state power for the 'Bahujan' majority.

questions.sub_topic: Disintegration of the 'Second World' and the Collapse of Bipolarity
questions.question: The dismantling of which concrete barrier on 9 November 1989 signaled the end of the Cold War divide in Europe?
questions.explanation: The fall of the Berlin Wall on 9 November 1989 marked the collapse of communist rule across East Germany and Eastern Europe.

questions.sub_topic: Disintegration of the 'Second World' and the Collapse of Bipolarity
questions.question: What Russian term meaning 'Openness' was introduced by Mikhail Gorbachev to allow political freedom of speech and expression in the Soviet Union?
questions.explanation: Glasnost (openness) was introduced by Gorbachev to permit open debate, freedom of expression, and transparency in government affairs.

questions.sub_topic: Disintegration of the 'Second World' and the Collapse of Bipolarity
questions.question: What international association of former Soviet republics was founded in December 1991 following the dissolution of the USSR?
questions.explanation: The Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS) was established in December 1991 by the leaders of Russia, Ukraine, and Belarus, later joined by other post-Soviet states.

questions.sub_topic: Alternative Centers of Economic and Political Power
questions.question: Which landmark treaty signed in 1992 formally established the European Union?
questions.explanation: The Maastricht Treaty was signed in the Netherlands in February 1992, creating the European Union and laying the foundation for the single currency.

questions.sub_topic: Alternative Centers of Economic and Political Power
questions.question: Which declaration was signed in August 1967 by the foreign ministers of five Southeast Asian nations to establish ASEAN?
questions.explanation: The Bangkok Declaration was signed on 8 August 1967 by Indonesia, Malaysia, Philippines, Singapore, and Thailand, founding ASEAN.

questions.sub_topic: Alternative Centers of Economic and Political Power
questions.question: Which Chinese leader introduced the 'Open Door Policy' in 1978 to attract foreign capital and technology into China?
questions.explanation: Deng Xiaoping announced the Open Door policy in December 1978, initiating market reforms and rapid export-led economic modernization.

questions.sub_topic: South Asia in the Post Cold War Era
questions.question: In which city is the permanent Secretariat of the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC) located?
questions.explanation: The SAARC Secretariat was established in Kathmandu, Nepal, on 16 January 1987 to coordinate the work of the association.

questions.sub_topic: South Asia in the Post Cold War Era
questions.question: Which separatist militant group led an armed conflict for an independent Tamil homeland in Sri Lanka from 1983 to 2009?
options: B) Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE)
C) Eelam People's Revolutionary Liberation Front
questions.explanation: The LTTE waged an armed civil war against the Sri Lankan government until its military defeat in May 2009.

questions.sub_topic: International Organisations in a Unipolar World
questions.question: Which body succeeded the League of Nations as the premier global international organisation on 24 October 1945?
options: D) The North Atlantic Treaty Organization
questions.explanation: The United Nations was established on 24 October 1945 by 51 founding member states as the successor to the League of Nations.

questions.sub_topic: International Organisations in a Unipolar World
questions.question: How many non-permanent members are elected to the United Nations Security Council for two-year terms?
questions.explanation: The UN Security Council consists of 5 permanent members (with veto power) and 10 non-permanent members elected by the General Assembly for two-year terms.

questions.question: What is the military strategy called where a state accumulates arms and builds alliances to prevent an adversary from attacking by threatening retaliation?
questions.explanation: Deterrence is the traditional security strategy of preventing war by demonstrating credible retaliatory force to make aggression too costly.

questions.sub_topic: Environment and Natural Resources in Global Politics
questions.question: Which international conference held in Rio de Janeiro in June 1992 is popularly known as the 'Earth Summit'?
options: A) Stockholm Conference on the Human Environment
B) United Nations Conference on Environment and Development (UNCED)
C) World Summit on Sustainable Development
questions.explanation: The UN Conference on Environment and Development (UNCED), known as the Earth Summit, produced Agenda 21, the Rio Declaration, and key environmental treaties in 1992.

questions.question: Where was the first global meeting of the World Social Forum (WSF) held in January 2001 to organize opposition to neo-liberal globalisation?
questions.explanation: The World Social Forum (WSF) convened its inaugural gathering in Porto Alegre, Brazil, in January 2001 under the banner 'Another World is Possible'.

questions.question: Which prominent socialist leader broke away from the Socialist Party to establish the Praja Socialist Party (PSP) in 1952?
options: D) J.B. Kripalani (merging Kisan Mazdoor Praja Party with the Socialist Party)
questions.explanation: In 1952, the Socialist Party merged with Acharya J.B. Kripalani's Kisan Mazdoor Praja Party (KMPP) to form the Praja Socialist Party (PSP).

questions.question: What was the popular movement in Maharashtra that agitated for a separate Marathi-speaking state between 1956 and 1960 called?
questions.explanation: The Samyukta Maharashtra Samiti, uniting socialists, communists, and regional leaders, campaigned for a separate Marathi state with Bombay as capital.

questions.question: What was the main purpose of the Community Development Programme (CDP) launched on 2 October 1952 across 55 pilot project blocks in India?
options: A) Nationalising all private agricultural farms across northern India
B) Promoting comprehensive rural community development, agriculture, health, and adult literacy through local participation
C) Replacing all state governments with central development boards
D) Constructing nuclear power stations in every rural district
questions.explanation: Launched in 1952, the CDP aimed at village reconstruction through self-help and state technical support in agriculture, health, education, and communications.

questions.question: Which international boundary between India and China in the western sector of Ladakh has been the subject of continuous territorial dispute since the 1950s?
options: C) Line of Actual Control (LAC) in the Aksai Chin region
questions.explanation: The boundary dispute in the western sector centers on Aksai Chin, where China constructed a strategic road connecting Tibet and Xinjiang in the late 1950s.

questions.sub_topic: Challenge to and Restoration of Congress System
questions.question: In the fourth General Election of 1967, which non-Congress coalition government was formed in Bihar under the Chief Ministership of Mahamaya Prasad Sinha?
questions.explanation: In Bihar, disparate opposition parties (SSP, PSP, Jana Sangh, and Jan Kranti Dal) united in 1967 to form an SVD coalition under Mahamaya Prasad Sinha.

questions.question: Which historic case decided by the Supreme Court in April 1976 (ADM Jabalpur) is widely regarded as the nadir of the Indian judiciary's defense of civil liberties during the Emergency?
options: A) Habeas Corpus case (ADM Jabalpur v. Shivkant Shukla)
questions.explanation: In ADM Jabalpur (1976), a 4:1 majority held that citizens could not seek habeas corpus relief against illegal detention during an emergency under Article 359.

questions.question: What was the key outcome of the 1986 Mizo Accord signed between Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi and Laldenga?
options: A) Mizoram was merged with Manipur to create a unified northeastern state
B) The MNF renounced violence and surrendered arms, and Mizoram was granted full statehood with special constitutional protections under Article 371G
C) Laldenga was appointed Governor of Assam while insurgency continued
D) Mizoram was placed under permanent direct central military rule
questions.explanation: The Mizo Accord (1986) brought two decades of armed conflict to an end, granting Mizoram statehood and constitutional safeguards under Article 371G.

questions.question: Which coalition government ruled India from 1996 to 1998, supported from the outside by the Congress Party?
options: C) The United Front government (headed by Deve Gowda and I.K. Gujral)
questions.explanation: The United Front, composed of regional parties and the Left Front, formed the government in 1996 with outside support from the Congress.

questions.sub_topic: Disintegration of the 'Second World' and the Collapse of Bipolarity
questions.question: What was the most severe immediate social impact of the free-market 'Shock Therapy' in Russia in the early 1990s?
options: A) The total eradication of all private enterprises across the country
B) The doubling of life expectancy for ordinary Russian citizens
C) The total abolition of all taxes and foreign trade deficits
D) Hyperinflation that destroyed people's savings, currency devaluation, and the dismantling of the social safety net
questions.explanation: Shock Therapy caused the ruble to plummet, inflation to soar, and state subsidies to vanish, throwing millions into poverty and creating powerful oligarchs.

questions.sub_topic: Alternative Centers of Economic and Political Power
questions.question: Which agreement concluded in 1985 eliminated systematic border controls among several European countries, allowing passport-free travel?
questions.explanation: The Schengen Agreement, signed in 1985 in Luxembourg, led to the creation of Europe's border-free Schengen Area with free movement of persons.

questions.sub_topic: South Asia in the Post Cold War Era
questions.question: In which year did the monarchy officially end in Nepal, transforming the country into a federal democratic republic?
questions.explanation: The newly elected Constituent Assembly of Nepal voted to abolish the 240-year-old Shah monarchy on 28 May 2008, declaring Nepal a federal democratic republic.

questions.sub_topic: Environment and Natural Resources in Global Politics
questions.question: What is the core principle enunciated in Principle 7 of the 1992 Rio Declaration that guides global climate negotiations?
options: A) Equal Per Capita Carbon Allocation
questions.explanation: CBDR recognizes that while all states share a common duty to protect the environment, developed states bear greater responsibility due to historical emissions and greater resources.

questions.question: Which dissenting Supreme Court judge in the ADM Jabalpur (1976) habeas corpus case upheld personal liberty, stating that Article 21 cannot be suspended, and was subsequently superseded for the post of Chief Justice of India?
questions.explanation: Justice H.R. Khanna's lone dissent upheld personal liberty during the Emergency; as punishment, the government superseded him in January 1977, appointing Justice M.H. Beg as CJI.

questions.sub_topic: Disintegration of the 'Second World' and the Collapse of Bipolarity
questions.question: On 8 December 1991, the leaders of which three Soviet republics signed the Belavezha Accords, formally declaring that the Soviet Union had ceased to exist as a subject of international law?
options: B) Russia (Boris Yeltsin), Ukraine (Leonid Kravchuk), and Belarus (Stanislav Shushkevich)
questions.explanation: The leaders of Russia, Ukraine, and Belarus met at Viskuli in Belovezha Forest and signed the historic accords terminating the USSR and establishing the CIS.

questions.sub_topic: Environment and Natural Resources in Global Politics
questions.question: Under the 1997 Kyoto Protocol, developing countries including India and China were classified as which group and exempt from binding greenhouse gas emissions reductions during the first commitment period?
questions.explanation: The Kyoto Protocol exempted developing countries (categorized as Non-Annex I parties) from binding emissions cuts during the first commitment period (2008-2012).
